title: Run History: inspect real journals and restore available settings
description: Find recorded jobs through Help, check settings, file inventories, warnings and failures, and reopen a real Recruitment configuration without rerunning or deleting anything.
objectives: Find Run history under Help and combine module, status and text filters.
Distinguish recorded file inventories and successful execution from scientific validation.
Read saved settings, environment details, warnings and an actual failure traceback.
Copy the journal path and restore available Recruitment controls without running analysis.
prerequisite: Use journals from your own completed example runs. This recording reads an isolated copy of the normal local journal location, ~/.spacr/runs, containing real tutorial jobs rather than fabricated results. The Batch Runner and Recruitment lessons explain the acquired test inputs; Regression supplies actual recorded warnings, and an earlier Model Zoo attempt supplies a real failure. Run History has no dedicated dataset download, live image preview, plotting or AI panel. No analysis, deletion or external file-manager launch is performed here. All 496 journal files remain byte-identical. The example restores 27 exposed Recruitment settings; the recorded hash_inputs key is not represented in that GUI. Recorded hashes describe the past run, not a fresh verification of today's project files.

scenes.narration: Open Help, then Run history. This shared tool reads the local run journal, not every project folder on your computer. We use genuine records from the other tutorial runs. You do not need to repeat those analyses just to inspect their history.

Refresh loads the available journal records. The table shows module, status, duration, CPU time and recorded file counts and sizes. Drag the divider to enlarge the detail area. These are saved execution measurements, not a live performance monitor or an independent assessment of scientific quality.

Choose convert and Success, then search for the shared example-folder name. Three actual Batch Runner jobs remain. Module, status and text filters work together; text search can find settings, paths, versions or recorded problems. There are no separate date or resource filters on this screen.

Files and models is empty for these successful conversions because their journal skipped file hashing. That does not mean they produced no images. The Batch Runner lesson separately checked all twelve outputs. Treat a missing inventory as missing evidence, not as proof of missing data.

An unmatched search leaves an empty table, clears the detail panes and disables selected-run actions. Restoring the previous search brings back the same three records. Check your filters before concluding that a run disappeared; this search does not delete journal files.

Now select the real Recruitment run. Overview shows about eighteen seconds elapsed and forty-five seconds of process CPU time; those are different measurements. Six input and six output file records are available. These counts describe recorded files, not cell numbers or a guarantee of complete inventory.

Settings displays the saved configuration, including source, channels, object filters and Plot enabled. Scroll to read the full snapshot. The source is the tutorial's private example project. These historical values do not automatically change if you edit the project or the current module settings later.

Files and models lists recorded paths, sizes and hashes when available. Inspect both inputs and outputs, and remember that the same database may have different before-and-after hashes. Opening history reads those saved records; it does not recompute every current file's hash or validate the biological result.

Environment includes recorded software versions, seed information and snapshot hashes. These help investigate differences between runs, but do not alone guarantee reproducibility. Copy path places this run's journal-folder path on the clipboard. Preserve its settings and manifest together with the separate project inputs and results.

A successful Regression record still has warnings about saved-figure contrast and missing provenance files. Warnings and failure separates those messages from a traceback. Success means execution finished; it does not certify readable figures, complete provenance or a valid statistical design. Read the dedicated Regression lesson for those checks.

The Failed filter exposes a genuine earlier Model Zoo attempt. Its traceback ends with an unsupported invert argument to Cellpose, which identifies a compatibility problem, not a segmentation result. We inspect the recorded failure without repeating it. Share relevant versions and error details when reporting a problem.

Return to Recruitment and choose Load settings in module. All twenty-seven available controls match the saved values, and no analysis starts. The journal also contains hash inputs, which is not represented in this form. Review restored settings and current inputs before running; this is not an exact replay guarantee.

Clear all deletes journal records; it is not a filter reset. We used neither that button nor the row menu's delete action, and every journal file stayed unchanged. For programmatic searches, use search_runs in spacr.run_journal. For a project report, use the separate Report lesson.
